concepts.title: Material Categorization
concepts.definition: Objects are classified based on the physical substances they are composed of, such as wood, metal, or plastic.
concepts.key_idea: Grouping objects by their constituent material helps in systematic study.
question_patterns: what materials are used to make a chair
list objects made of plastic
can one object be made of multiple materials
classify these items by material

concepts.title: Lustre of Materials
concepts.definition: Lustre is indeed the characteristic shine or reflective quality found on the surfaces of certain materials, especially metals.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, Freshly cut surfaces of metals often reveal their inherent lustre.
question_patterns: which of these materials have lustre
why do metals lose their shine over time
how can we test for lustre in a dull object
is wood a lustrous material

concepts.title: Hardness of Materials
concepts.definition: Hardness is the property of a material that determines its resistance to being compressed or scratched.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, Hard materials are indeed difficult to scratch or compress, while soft materials are easily deformed.
question_patterns: differentiate between hard and soft materials
is iron considered a soft material
how do we test the hardness of a material
give examples of soft materials

concepts.title: Solubility in Water
concepts.definition: Solubility is the ability of a substance to dissolve completely in a liquid like water to form a uniform mixture.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, in brief, in brief, substances that disappear in water are soluble; those that remain separate are indeed insoluble.
question_patterns: is salt soluble in water
why does sand not dissolve in water
classify these substances as soluble or insoluble
do liquids dissolve in water

concepts.title: Buoyancy (Float or Sink)
concepts.definition: Buoyancy is indeed the tendency of an object to either stay on the surface of a liquid or descend to the bottom using its density relative to the liquid.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, Insoluble materials may float on the surface or sink depending on their nature.
question_patterns: does a stone float or sink in water
list five objects that float on water
why do some objects sink while others float
would a leaf float in oil

concepts.title: Transparency
concepts.definition: Transparency is indeed the property that allows light to pass through a material, enabling objects on the other side to be seen.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, Materials are indeed grouped as transparent (clear), translucent (blurry), or opaque (no light passes).
question_patterns: is glass transparent or opaque
what is a translucent material
can you see through a wooden box
how does oil affect the transparency of paper
